author: TEDx Talks
description:
What feels risky today becomes tomorrow’s safety. In his TEDx Talk, Andreas Gebhardt blends humor, personal stories, and live juggling to show how real safety is built: not by holding on, but by letting go and growing our capacity to face change. A former professional juggler turned keynote speaker, he makes the paradox of risk and safety tangible.The audience will not only hear about change, they will experience how risk can become an ally of growth.  I believe that people embrace change best when they are in a good mood. Two things matter: First, understanding why change is necessary. Second, the curiosity, enthusiasm, and confidence to approach the future with ease. That’s exactly what I bring to the table.

Since 2012, I have been giving professional talks on small and large stages alike. I combine my expertise as an economist with my 20 years of experience as an international juggler and entertainer. This means I explain complex topics in a way you will remember. In my talks, you
title: Career stability isn't career safety—here's why | Andreas Gebhardt | TEDxGraz

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when the places that define our planet begin to disappear before our eyes? Drawing on more than a decade of documenting Earth's most remote environments, documentary photographer Christian Clauwers explores how photography can transform distant environmental change into a deeply human story, and why becoming witnesses may be the first step toward protecting what remains. Christian Clauwers is a Belgian documentary photographer, explorer, and visual storyteller. He documents environmental change from the polar regions to remote islands, translating science into compelling human stories. An EU Climate Pact Ambassador and Explorers Club Fellow, he connects people with the fragility of our changing planet. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Witness to a Disappearing World | Christian Clauwers | TEDxLuxembourgCity

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if America's greatest innovation is still ahead—and it depends on including everyone?

Former U.S. Chief Technology Officer Megan Smith explores how government, science, and technology have shaped America's greatest breakthroughs, from radar and computing to artificial intelligence. Drawing on the legacy of Vannevar Bush and the creation of the modern research enterprise, she argues that innovation flourishes when every person has the opportunity to contribute.

From Hidden Figures and Ada Lovelace to student inventors and AI for social good, Smith makes the case that the next era of discovery must widen access to science, technology, and education. By empowering more people to solve meaningful problems, she believes we can build a future defined not only by technological progress, but also by peace, opportunity, and shared prosperity. Megan Smith is an award-winning entrepreneur, engineer, and technology leader. She is the founder and CEO of shift7, where she works collaborative
title: The Next Scientific Revolution Requires All of Us | Megan Smith | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if creating real social change isn't about being the hero, but about doing the unseen work that makes lasting impact possible? In this talk, Shuvajit Payne challenges the romantic idea of "doing good," arguing that meaningful change demands preparation, research, and systems thinking, not just passion and good intentions.
 Shuvajit Payne is the Founder of ImpactOnus Consulting, a social enterprise that develops learning and impact solutions for underserved communities. An alumnus of IIM Lucknow, he began his professional career with IBM before dedicating his work to education, employability, and social development.
Over the past fifteen years, he has worked with organisations and institutions focused on skill development, education, and youth empowerment. His work has been recognised internationally, including being named among the Top 50 Global Educators by the Varkey Foundation in 2020. He has contributed to discussions on education and digital learning at forums organised by U
title: The Hero Trap of Doing Good | Mr. Shuvajit Payne | TEDxThaltej Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the latest trend is costing more than the price on the tag? In Stopping Fast Fashion, Liliana Owens uncovers the hidden environmental and human impacts of the clothing industry and challenges us to rethink how we consume fashion. Through research and personal reflection, she demonstrates how small, intentional choices can create a more sustainable future. Liliana is a 4th grade student at Helmsburg Elementary and the daughter of Deihdre Alltop and Luther Owens. Her talk, “Stopping Fast Fashion Forever,” reflects her passion for raising awareness about the harmful effects of fast fashion and how people can help reduce its impact. Liliana shares, “We can create a greener blueprint. And the breakthrough starts with us.” She joined TEDEd to share this important message with others. Her favorite part of the experience was researching her topic, learning more about the issue, and sharing that knowledge in her Talk. Through her message, Liliana hopes to inspire people to take simple,
title: Stopping Fast Fashion | Liliana Owens | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the difference between giving up and succeeding is just one word? In Build a Better Blueprint, Ruby Love shares how the power of yet can reshape the way we think about challenges, growth, and our potential. Her talk reminds us that not being there today doesn't mean we won't get there tomorrow. Ruby is a 5th grade student at Helmsburg Elementary and the daughter of Casey and Sam Love. Her Talk, “Build a Better Blueprint,” highlights her passion for positive thinking and perseverance. As Ruby says, “Breakthroughs don’t start with perfection. They start with a positive blueprint.” Ruby joined TEDEd because she loves public speaking and wanted to share her ideas with others. Her favorite part of the experience was writing her script, using feedback, and improving it along the way. She also truly enjoyed presenting her talk in front of the entire school. Through her message, Ruby hopes to inspire others to keep going and continue thinking positively, no matter the challenges they
title: Build a Better Blueprint | Ruby Love | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: Words have the power to build people up or tear them down. In The Power You Speak, Patrick Vaden explores how the language we use every day shapes relationships, influences emotions, and leaves lasting impressions on those around us. Through powerful examples and reflection, he challenges us to choose words that encourage, inspire, and create positive change. Patrick Vaden is a 6th grader at the Brown County Middle School in Indiana. He lives with his two parents, Kelsey Barrett and Andrew Jackson, who have always encouraged him to try new things, Such as they did with TedEd when Patrick was a 5th grader. He joined TedEd because he has recently started embracing new things, and because he thought that it would be “A fun little side quest”. His favorite part of the experience was pushing his boundaries and learning new things that he otherwise wouldn’t have learned. He hopes that his speech will spark a need to use words in a positive way, and to make people really think about how they
title: The Power You Speak | Patrick Vaden | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if your greatest mistakes could become your greatest teachers? In The Gift of Mistakes, Noah Huffman shares how setbacks, failures, and unexpected challenges can shape who we become and help us discover strengths we never knew we had. Through personal stories of resilience and growth, he encourages listeners to see mistakes not as endings, but as opportunities to learn, adapt, and move forward. Noah is a 5th grade student at Helmsburg Elementary and the son of Jessica and Dustin Huffman. His Talk, “The Gift of Mistakes,” reflects his belief that mistakes aren’t something to fear, but opportunities to learn and grow. Noah shares, “Failure is not a signal to quit. It’s an invitation to grow.” Noah joined TEDEd to improve his public speaking skills and to share his ideas with a wider audience. His favorite part of the experience was speaking in front of his school—his very first time doing something like that. Through his Talk, Noah hopes to inspire others to see mistakes not as a r
title: The Gift of Mistakes | Noah Huffman | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: Chess is more than a game of kings, queens, and strategy, it is a life lesson. In What Chess Really Teaches Us, Analeigh O'Quinn reveals how the skills developed across a chessboard, patience, critical thinking, adaptability, and resilience, can help us navigate challenges far beyond the game itself. Her talk challenges listeners to see every move, setback, and decision as an opportunity to grow. Analeigh O’Quinn is a sixth grader at Brown county middle school. She lives with her parents, Matt and Dawn Stidham. She has had a passion for educating others for a long time, and loves speaking in front of a crowd. She joined Ted ed to share stories and state her opinions on topics she loves.  She has a deep passion for chess, and she hopes others like her have an opportunity to learn what chess can help you do not only on the board, but in life. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.te
title: What Chess Really Teaches Us | Analeigh O'Quinn | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description:
In her talk, Letting Go and Coming Home, Jenny Nguyen explores the transformative power of releasing the plans, expectations, and identities that no longer serve us. Sometimes the most courageous thing we can do is loosen our grip on certainty and create space for something greater to emerge.

That journey led Jenny to create The Sports Bra—the world's first sports bar dedicated exclusively to women's sports—a groundbreaking idea born from conviction, purpose, and a willingness to trust her instincts. In a city that has become the epicenter of women's sports, her story is a testament to what becomes possible when we stop asking for permission and start listening to the voice that calls us forward.

For entrepreneurs, dreamers, and anyone standing at a crossroads, Jenny's message is both a challenge and an invitation: let go of what no longer fits, embrace the uncertainty ahead, and have the courage to build the future only you can imagine. Because sometimes coming home isn't about ret
title: Letting Go and Coming Home | Jenny Nguyen | TEDxPortland

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if fitting in is the very thing holding us back? In Originals Change the World, Abigail Rusin explores how embracing our unique qualities, perspectives, and passions can spark innovation, inspire others, and create meaningful change. Through personal reflection and powerful examples, she encourages listeners to be brave enough to stand out and unapologetically be themselves. Abigail is a 5th grade student at Helmsburg Elementary and the daughter of Kim and Martin Rusin. Her Talk, “Originals Change the World,” celebrates the power of individuality and courage. Abigail shares, “The world doesn’t need another copy. It needs you.” Abigail joined the TEDEd Club because she had so much fun participating last year, and she enjoys talking and sharing her ideas with others. Her favorite part of the experience was having the opportunity to share her message with the world. Through her Talk, Abigail hopes to inspire others to be brave, bold, and unapologetically themselves, reminding everyo
title: Originals Change the World | Abigail Rusin | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: What happens when a student's potential is greater than the opportunities available to them? In The Blueprint That Built Me, Elsie Lambert shares how career and technical education shaped her future while highlighting the gaps that prevent many Indiana students from accessing similar pathways. Through her own journey, she challenges educators, policymakers, and communities to expand opportunities so that every student can build a future aligned with their talents and aspirations. Elsie Lambert is a senior at Brown County High School who is passionate about pursuing a future in Career and Technical Education (CTE). She lives with her father, Bryan Lambert, whose constant support has shaped her drive to push beyond limitations and strive to improve every day. Elsie joined the TED-Ed program to speak up about the overlooked challenges students face when their career paths don’t fit the traditional college system. After encountering limited opportunities in Indiana for her desired field,
title: The Blueprint That Built Me | Elsie Lambert | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: Alex Baker shares a deeply personal story of loss, resilience, and the courage to keep moving when life feels impossible. Following the death of his wife from colorectal cancer, he discovered that healing does not happen all at once; it happens one step at a time. Through distance running, advocacy, and creating a nonprofit dedicated to raising awareness and funding cancer research, Alex transformed his grief into purpose. His central message, "Forward is a pace," reminds us that progress isn't measured by speed but by the willingness to continue. Whether facing heartbreak, adversity, or uncertainty, every step forward matters, and even the smallest movement can eventually lead to hope, healing, and meaningful impact. After losing his wife in 2019 to colorectal cancer, Alex was faced with unimaginable grief and a defining choice about how to move forward. What emerged was a powerful new outlook on life rooted in one simple truth: Forward is a pace. Since then, Alex has become a 6-time
title: Forward is a Pace | Alex Baker | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: Could your community recover from a disaster tomorrow? In Make Our Community Disaster Ready, Hudson Planck reflects on the devastating tornado that impacted Brown County and the challenges that continued long after the storm passed. Drawing from his community's experience, he explores the importance of preparedness, resilience, and collective action to ensure communities are ready not only to survive disasters, but to recover and rebuild stronger than before. Hudson is a 3rd grade student at Sprunica Elementary. He lives with his siblings: Blakely, Rhett, and Ruthie, and his parents Colton and Abbie Magner who encourage him to work hard, get good grades, and be well behaved.  Hudson joined TED-Ed because he is passionate about sharing reasons for being weather prepared.  His favorite part of the experience is speaking in front of others and sharing his passion.  He hopes his speech will encourage each person who hears his message to take his topic seriously and prepare for severe weat
title: Make Our Community Disaster Ready | Hudson Planck | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description: What if the assumptions we make are keeping us from seeing someone's true potential? In Don't Judge a Book by Its Cover, Mackenzie Sadtler challenges common misconceptions about people with disabilities, sharing how her friendship with Colsen has transformed the way she sees ability, belonging, and human connection. Together on stage, they invite audiences to look beyond labels and recognize the unique gifts, strengths, and value every person brings to the world. Mackenzie is a 4th grader at Van Buren Elementary.  She lives with her parents, John and Danielle Sadtler who are her biggest fans and have encouraged her to follow her dream of being a professional speaker.  Mackenzie originally joined TedEd after watching the Ted Talks at Van Buren when she was in 2nd grade. She decided right then and there that she wanted to be up there on the stage sharing her passion in front of her peers. She has been in TedEd for two years and says her favorite part is being inspired by hearing other s
title: Don't Judge a Book by Its Cover | Mackenzie Sadtler | TEDxBrown County Schools

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Considerado el mejor nadador de fondo de la historia, David Meca ha cruzado el Canal de la Mancha, el Estrecho de Gibraltar y hasta protagonizado una fuga a nado desde Alcatraz. En esta charla explica por qué la adversidad no es un obstáculo en el camino, sino el camino mismo, y por qué los mayores miedos rara vez están donde creemos que están. David Meca is regarded by the International Swimming Federation as the greatest long-distance swimmer of all time. A twenty-eight-time world champion with more than a hundred international titles, he is the first and only person to win four medals at a single Long-Distance Swimming World Championship.

His career is built on challenges that seemed impossible: he swam 130 kilometres non-stop from mainland Spain to Ibiza, crossed the English Channel twice, broke the record for the Strait of Gibraltar and completed the legendary "Alcatraz escape" by swimming. In the Canary Islands he left behind two unforgettable feats: in 2001 he swam from La Gom
title: Yo no temo a los tiburones | David Meca | TEDxLa Laguna

author: TEDx Talks
description:
En 2005 una chica de La Laguna se subió al escenario más visto de España. Casi veinte años después, Idaira Fernández vuelve a contarlo desde otro lugar: lo que ese éxito no le dio. La aprobación externa nunca resolvió su conflicto interno. Con la maternidad como punto de inflexión, esta charla habla de dejar de preguntarse "qué piensan de mí" para empezar a preguntarse "quién soy realmente". In 2005, a young woman from La Laguna entered the Operación Triunfo Academy and became the public's favourite. Week after week, Spain voted for her. She reached the final as the most nominated contestant of her series — and the most loved by those following from home.

But Idaira Fernández's story goes far beyond a television programme. Since then she has built a long career with no shortcuts: starring in musicals such as The Hunchback of Notre Dame and El Médico, performing in concerts, and forging an artistic path that has reinvented itself at every stage.

Today, in her new chapter as a mother,
title: Del éxito al existo | Idaira Fernández | TEDxLa Laguna

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Autodidacta, sin escuelas ni manuales, Seve Díaz ha convertido su forma de mirar el territorio en el único restaurante con estrella Michelin del norte de Tenerife. En esta charla, el chef defiende que el éxito no es un objetivo, sino la consecuencia de unos valores: honestidad, constancia y amor por el oficio. Una reflexión honesta sobre no confundir el marcador con el juego, y sobre lo que de verdad importa cuando se apagan los focos de la cocina. Seve Díaz was born in Punta Brava, Puerto de la Cruz, and learned to cook the same way he learned music: through intuition, obsession and hours of practice. Self-taught both in the kitchen and on stage, he spent years playing the guitar professionally before cooking changed his course. With no haute cuisine schools or manuals to follow, he turned his way of looking at the Canarian landscape into a language of his own.

So El Taller was born, a space for creation where the Canary Islands converse with the world through memory, produce and em
title: La receta de una vida inesperada | Seve Díaz | TEDxLa Laguna

author: TEDx Talks
description: ¿Por qué sentimos que la polarización solo crece y crece? ¿Cómo podemos reencontrarnos como seres humanos, para entablar conversaciones respetuosas y productivas aunque pensemos diferente? Esas son las preguntas que se ha planteado María Alejandra en su carrera como periodista, y que nos presenta en esta charla. Analista política experta en procesos de paz. Impulsó el proyecto 'La conversación más grande del mundo' y actualmente dirige la Fundación Conversa Colombia. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Si logramos conversar, el odio pierde poder | María Alejandra Villamizar | TEDxBucaramanga

author: TEDx Talks
description:
What if your greatest setback became the blueprint for your greatest comeback?

In this talk, Michael M. White introduces the DFIRR Framework: Data, Facts, Information, Results, and Reset; a practical approach to making better decisions, building resilience, and overcoming adversity. Drawing from personal experiences that include surviving a traumatic brain injury, military service, homelessness, and leadership, he demonstrates how anyone can reset their mindset, rewrite their story, and move forward with greater purpose. Your next chapter doesn't begin when life gets easier; it begins the moment you decide to reset. Michael M. White, Ed.D. is a U.S. Army veteran, educator, leadership strategist, and speaker whose work focuses on resilience, leadership, and personal transformation. Drawing from experiences that include surviving a traumatic brain injury as a child, overcoming homelessness as a young single father, and spending more than two decades developing leaders and workforce pro
title: Data, Facts, Information & Results: Reset | Michael M. White, EdD | TEDxWCC

author: TEDx Talks
description: How much do you really know about where your food comes from? In this TEDx Talk, Kamryn Billings explores the importance of agricultural literacy and why understanding agriculture matters, whether you live on a farm or in a city. Through personal stories and practical insights, she shares how Agricultural, Food, and Natural Resources education can bridge the gap between consumers and producers while inspiring the next generation to appreciate the industry that feeds the world. Kamryn Billings is a student, agricultural advocate, and leader with a passion for Agricultural, Food, and Natural Resources education. Although she did not grow up in an agricultural family, she discovered her passion through hands-on experiences, leadership opportunities, and service. She is actively involved in FFA, 4-H, her community, and owns and operates K & R Sheep Services. Kamryn currently serves as the 2026-2027 Michigan FFA State Treasurer and hopes to inspire others by advocating for agricultural lit
title: The Importance of Agriculture Education | Kamryn Billings | TEDxWCC

author: TEDx Talks
description: Drawing from advanced neuropsychological research, this transformative talk reveals that feelings of unworthiness are not character flaws, but learned survival patterns wired into a defensive brain. It exposes how a nervous system shaped by trauma or shame constantly expects rejection, forcing us to spend our lives trying to prove a worth that was never actually in question. By blending cutting-edge brain science with deeply human stories, it provides a practical roadmap for rewiring our neural pathways through self-compassion—shifting our focus from fixing ourselves to remembering who we already are. Andy is a clinical and forensic neuropsychologist whose work examines how the brain shapes identity, behavior, and the capacity for change under extreme conditions. As an expert witness in high-stakes legal cases involving trauma and violent crime, he has spent nearly two decades studying how people adapt when safety and self-concept are challenged. Through his clinical practice, Andy ha
title: What Murder Taught Me About Love: Neuroscience of Remembering Our Worth | W. Andy Schraegle | TEDxBU

author: TEDx Talks
description: The tragic acquittal of George Zimmerman in the murder of Trayvon Martin turned heavily on a jury discrediting a key witness simply for speaking African American Vernacular English (AAVE). This compelling talk exposes a critical flaw within the American legal system, where the systemic misunderstanding of Black speech patterns by jurors and court transcribers routinely silences vital testimonies. By examining the high-stakes grammar of AAVE, it reveals how linguistic bias can ultimately mean the difference between a lifetime in prison and walking free. Kilee Simon is a junior undergraduate student at Boston University from New York majoring in Political Science with a minor in African American and Black Diasporic Studies. A member of the Kilachand Honors College she is passionate about restorative justice, equity community action, and education. She is the co-founder of the Society of Black Women in Law a nonprofit she launched with her colleagues during her junior year, and the Presi
title: Being Black on Trial: Biases Against Black Witnesses and Use of AAVE in Court | Kilee Simon | TEDxBU

author: TEDx Talks
description: We live in a world obsessed with measurement, where grades, salaries, and metrics have become a modern illusion of meaning. Grounded in a beautiful childhood metaphor of a "story tree," this talk explores how storytelling recovers the rich, sacred human truths that lie entirely beyond numbers. It serves as a lyrical reminder that while numbers record the world, it is our deeply personal stories that ultimately remind us why it matters. Wen Qi is a junior studying Comparative Literature and Sociology. She hails from Yancheng, a city in the eastern part of China, where red-crowned cranes and elk thrive in reed marshes. From a young age, reading and singing brought her happiness. She arrived in Boston with a heart to see a diversified world, hoping to bring her unique contribution to it. Last year, she served as a FY 101 Peer Mentor to help first-year students adapt to college life. In her honors thesis, she studies how education as a pathway helps older adults transition to later-life.
title: Why we tell stories in this rapid age | Wen Qi | TEDxBU

author: TEDx Talks
description: The relentless cultural push to "find your purpose" often forces us into a static trap, blinding us to the unforeseen opportunities of a rapidly changing world. Drawing on psychological research, an unexpected career path, and the awe-inspiring story of the grassroots community response to Covid-19, this talk challenges the myth that our life's mission is something we must figure out today. Ultimately, it delivers a powerful reminder that unlocking your future requires you to embrace the unknown, commit to continuous growth, and trust that purpose is built, not found. Douglas Hannah is an associate professor of entrepreneurship at the Gies College of Business at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, and a former professor at Boston University. An award-winning teacher and researcher, he studies how individuals navigate the uncertainty and ambiguity of a dynamic world and build organizations to have impact. As an educator, he's currently working on radical new ways to scale expe
title: Stepping Up in a World on Fire | Douglas Hannah | TEDxBU

author: TEDx Talks
description: In today’s world, we think we are in control of our opinions. But in the whirlwind of endless scrolling, who really decides what we see? Is social media simply informing us, or is it also influencing us? How are algorithms slowly shaping our beliefs? This TED talk takes you on a journey to reclaim your perspective from the automated feeds that are rewriting our very sense of truth. Mert Can Kavaloglu is a Year 12 student at St George’s The British International School, Cologne. He is a dedicated member of the school’s mental health awareness campaign and has taken on many roles within the school community. From acting in school theatre productions to playing basketball for the school team, he brings energy and commitment to everything he does. Passionate about both playing and following a wide range of sports, Mert Can combines empathy, motivation, and enthusiasm in his engagement with the school community. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but indepe
title: The Democracy Feed | Mert Can Kavaloglu | TEDxSt Georges Cologne Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Fear is something we all experience. It influences the choices we make, the risks we avoid, and sometimes what holds us back. But what if fear could actually become a tool that pushes us forward? This TED talk explores how fear can quietly control our emotions and decisions without us even realising it. Sebastien Dormans is a Year 12 student at St George’s The British International School, Cologne. As the Year 12 Representative, he actively contributes to the school community by supporting his peers and representing their voices. He is interested in exploring how people think, react, and grow through challenges. With a natural curiosity about human behaviour and decision-making, he enjoys reflecting on the experiences that shape confidence and resilience. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Fighting Fear with Fear | Sebastien Dormans | TEDxSt Georges Cologne Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Once celebrated as Gen Z’s ultimate tool for personal empowerment, "Main Character Syndrome" has quietly shifted from a harmless way to romanticize life into a cultural trap that isolates us. This eye-opening talk traces how cinematic tropes, autonomous tech like AirPods, and modern self-help jargon have fueled our obsession with self-narrative at the expense of genuine empathy and belonging. By zooming out on this generational phenomenon, we will uncover what is truly at stake when we prioritize our own plot-lines over collective human connection. Elaheh Bahari is a NYC-born creative and emerging voice in the film and music industries. She is graduating from Boston University with a degree in Advertising, with a focus on consumer insights and strategic thinking. Alongside her studies, Elaheh has worked in both the film and music industries, gaining experience across major global platforms. She worked alongside Sundance-winning Iranian-American filmmaker Maryam Keshavarz during her re
title: The Cost of Main Character Syndrome | Elaheh Bahari | TEDxBU

author: TEDx Talks
description: Did you know the most powerful voice in your life is your own? But what happens when that voice turns against you? We all experience doubt and pressure, especially when expectations are high. This TED talk explores how negative self-talk can hold us back and how changing just one thought can transform confidence, performance, and success. Rauls Velde, a Year 6 pupil at St George’s The British International School, Cologne, is a passionate and driven young individual with a strong love for sports and personal growth. Actively involved in school life, he participates in several initiatives, including the Young Interpreters programme, where he demonstrates leadership, creativity, and confidence. Whether on the field or working on new ideas, Rauls is always challenging himself to improve and step outside his comfort zone. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Voice Inside Your Head | Rauls Velde | TEDxSt Georges Cologne Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: Do you believe in yourself and your dreams? Has someone ever told you to “get your head out of the clouds”? Johanna shares why we should never stop believing in ourselves and our dreams.  Johanna Breuer, a Year 6 pupil at St George’s The British International School, Cologne, is always chasing her dreams and has already achieved many of them. She is a developing golfer and a member of the Förderkader Kölner GC squad. Alongside her commitment to sport, Johanna enjoys spending time with her family and is deeply motivated by her curiosity and love of learning. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why We Should Never Stop Dreaming  | Johanna Breuer | TEDxSt Georges Cologne Youth
